pairs.subject: bounded-enumeration
pairs.evidence: apps/console/src/pages/reconcile/NoReport.tsx:11 The empty-state page reads the whole tournament collection through the limit-less, bare-array `tournament.list` (EmptyParams -> Vec<TournamentRow>, one row per sim directory, so it grows with every tournament run) and reduces all of it client-side to pick the newest, even though a paged `tournaments.page` exists; that read has no bound and no continuation.

techniques.evidence: apps/console/src/pages/reconcile/NoReport.tsx:11 This is a limit-unaware full-list caller of a collection that keeps growing. The bare-array reply has no place for a continuation, so once a limit lands this caller will either fail or silently truncate. By contrast, Incidents.tsx:76 in the same context does it right: it pages on the daemon's `more`/`next_cursor` continuation, not on a short page.

apps/console/src/pages/reconcile/Incidents.tsx:69 The only filter here is a `rule` facet the operator picks, applied as a server query predicate. Nothing hides keys per caller for access reasons, so the technique's precondition does not hold.

crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/report_wire.rs:66 The paged collection (a stored report's incidents) is immutable, so no write can land mid-walk. The anchor is on the daemon side of the endpoint this context pages.
crates/shadowrunr-types/src/rpc.rs:194 The ceiling is one fixed contract constant. No policy layer states list capabilities or ceilings that would need merging, and there is no recursive list verb.
